questions.question: WebSocket drops on mobile networks. What is your client reconnection and message delivery strategy?
questions.title: WebSocket Reconnect — Backoff, Idempotency, and Missed Messages
questions.direct_answer:
WebSocket drops on mobile networks. What is your client reconnection and message delivery strategy?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser, network, and server contract (headers, cookies, streams)), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Backoff, heartbeat/ping-pong, dedupe keys, ordering guarantees, STOMP if applicable.

**Classic weak answer:** Reconnecting instantly in a tight loop—DoS your own gateway.

**Senior finish:** Mention **circuit breaker** on server and **rate limits** for reconnect storms after deploy.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **WebSocket Reconnect — Backoff, Idempotency, and Missed Messages** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** WebSocket drops on mobile networks. What is your client reconnection and message delivery strategy?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **Backoff, heartbeat/ping-pong, dedupe keys, ordering guarantees, STOMP if applicable**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Reconnecting instantly in a tight loop—DoS your own gateway**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Mention **circuit breaker** on server and **rate limits** for reconnect storms after deploy**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** Backoff, heartbeat/ping-pong, dedupe keys, ordering guarantees, STOMP if applicable
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.title: Mental model (flowchart)
sections.content:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Connecting
    Connecting --> Open: handshake OK
    Open --> Degraded: heartbeat missed
    Degraded --> Reconnecting: backoff + jitter
    Reconnecting --> Open: resume / replay
    Open --> Closed: app teardown
    Reconnecting --> Closed: max attempts
    Closed --> [*]
```

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **reconnecting instantly in a tight loop—DoS your own gateway** and what you do instead.

sections.title: Key points (memorize this list)
sections.content:
- **Headline definition** in one sentence.
- **Mechanism:** Backoff, heartbeat/ping-pong, dedupe keys, ordering guarantees, STOMP if applicable
- **Pitfall:** Reconnecting instantly in a tight loop—DoS your own gateway
- **Differentiator:** Mention **circuit breaker** on server and **rate limits** for reconnect storms after deploy
- **Proof:** DevTools / Network / Performance trace, test strategy, or metric.
- **Close:** decision rule + sensible follow-up question back to the interviewer.

sections.title: How to answer verbally (timed)
sections.content:
**Open (15–20 seconds):** Restate the question and give the one-sentence definition.

**Body (45–60 seconds):** Walk through **Backoff, heartbeat/ping-pong, dedupe keys, ordering guarantees, STOMP if applicable** as a story: what runs, what breaks, what you log/measure.

**Pitfall (15 seconds):** Call out **Reconnecting instantly in a tight loop—DoS your own gateway** — interviewers reward honesty about real bugs.

**Finish (15–20 seconds):** Add **Mention **circuit breaker** on server and **rate limits** for reconnect storms after deploy**, then offer a trade-off question back (“do you optimize for TTFB or TTI here?”).
